about.title: About — Tim Chen
about.description: Tim Chen is a C#/.NET backend engineer. This page covers how he works, language study in Japan and JLPT N1, and an engineering reading group.
about.heading: About
about.lead: Yu-Ting Chen. I use C# and .NET to make existing backends faster, more reliable, and safer to change.
about.engineering: Since March 2026 I have been developing .NET backend services and improving existing systems at Gogoro. Before that, from August 2020 to April 2023, I was a Product Developer at Titansoft, working on REST and gRPC microservices. I also interned there in 2020.
about.projects: The things I build for myself stay small. The longer thread is time and self-discipline: Level, TimeMiner, and Discipline App. The other thread is small tools I keep opening.
about.japan: From 2024 to 2025 I studied at a Japanese language school and have passed JLPT N1. That is language study and cross-cultural learning. It is not Japanese work experience, and it is not native business fluency.
about.sharing: At Titansoft I organized an engineering reading group so we could talk through practical problems and compare approaches.
about.life: Outside work I ride, hike, and like seeing one thing through.

work.description: Tim Chen's portfolio: de-identified backend work cases, and public projects that can be opened now.
work.title: Work
work.lead: The work cases are above, and each number has a scope. Below that are my own things. They are small, and I use them.
work.case1Title: A checksum mismatch caused extra fallback calls
work.case1Problem: When the checksum did not match, the system called a fallback API again. Those calls were about 75,000 a day, and most of them were unnecessary.
work.case1Action: I found and fixed the checksum mismatch so those fallback calls were no longer sent.
work.case1Result: Daily calls for this fallback fell from about 75,000 to fewer than 50.
work.case1Scope: The metric is the call volume of this fallback, not the system-wide error rate, operating cost, or all API traffic.
work.case2Problem: Some API responses took over 2 seconds, so callers had to wait.
work.case2Action: I improved the performance of the APIs that were actually slow.
work.case2Result: After the change, those responses were about 200 milliseconds.
work.case2Scope: This covers only the APIs that were changed, not every API and not the whole platform. p95/p99, sample size, and test conditions were not provided.
work.case3Title: Station maintenance notices were hard to test
work.case3Problem: Calculation and service responsibilities were mixed together, and time was hard to replace, so aggregating station data, merging time ranges, and caching were difficult to check on their own.
work.case3Action: I separated calculation from the service, injected a time dependency, and added tests around aggregation, range merging, and caching.
work.case3Result: That behavior can now be protected by tests, so later changes rely less on manual regression. Over the same period the existing unit-test suite grew from 41 to 240 (the total on 2026-10-01), and tests that had been failing were fixed.
work.case3Scope: 240 is the suite total, not 240 tests written from scratch, and not a coverage percentage. Internal API paths, service names, and station identifiers are not published here.
work.publicLead: The first two are things I open: a focus timer, and the small tools on this site. The next two are C# exercises where you can see how the code is layered.
work.disciplineBody: I wanted a focus timer I would actually open. It has a Pomodoro timer and daily tasks, experience points when I finish, and a connection to the Google Calendar and Google Tasks I already use. It uses ASP.NET Core Blazor Server, .NET 7, Entity Framework Core, and SQLite. Sign-in is Google OAuth. It runs on Azure App Service and is published with GitHub Actions.
work.disciplineScope: It is one personal site. The demo currently loads.
work.twstockBody: A small service for Taiwan stock data. I split it into Api, Application, Domain, and Infrastructure so data can be collected, stored, and queried. It uses ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, SQL Server LocalDB, and Swagger. The data comes from the TWSE and FinMind. The domain has unit tests. The frontend is Next.js.
work.twstockScope: There is no deployed site. The source is the place to look.
work.yungchingBody: A product API made before an interview at Yung Ching Realty. It stays on GitHub because they said it could be published, and because the layering, validation, and tests are visible there. It uses ASP.NET Core 7, Entity Framework Core, SQLite, AutoMapper, FluentValidation, and Swagger.
work.yungchingScope: They said it could be published.
work.toolsBody: When I need a timestamp, formatted JSON, or a look at a JWT, I open this page. Timestamp, JSON, YAML, hashes, encoding, JWT, URL, UUID, regular expressions, and base conversion run in the browser after the page loads, and there are tests.
work.toolsScope: The stack is HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
work.historyLead: Level and TimeMiner came before Discipline App. I wanted time and self-discipline to live somewhere I would open.
work.timeminerBody: The earlier work-time log. It manages custom tables and records work time, with ASP.NET Core MVC and Entity Framework Core, on Azure.
work.levelBody: An earlier self-discipline app, built with Flutter and Firebase. It was on Google Play. The store page no longer opens. The source is still there.
work.award: In 2019 a university project, done with classmates, placed third in Information Applications at the International ICT Innovative Services Awards.
work.asideBody: In 2024–2025 I studied at a language school in Tokyo and passed JLPT N1. While I was in Japan I built a Japanese vocabulary practice site with Flask. At Titansoft I ran an engineering reading group. Outside work I ride, hike, and like seeing one thing through.
